entries.message: expected a component element and received {received}.
entries.fix: Pass the element whose loop is intentional — `allowRenderLoop(this)` inside the component.

entries.message: returned a promise — an async callback runs, but it cannot return a cleanup, and what it awaits may arrive after the component re-ran or was removed.
entries.fix: To cancel it, write the effect as a plain function that starts the async work and returns a cleanup that stops it — for a fetch, `const c = new AbortController(); load(c.signal); return () => c.abort();`.

entries.message: render() was called with no template. That works — the setup is committed and the hooks run, exactly as with a template — but mount() is the name for it, and says so at the call site.
expected a component element and received {received}.
entries.fix: Call it in connectedCallback with the component itself — `init(this)`.

entries.message: called init() twice in one setup, so the {hooks} hook(s) registered since the first call were discarded and will never run.
entries.fix: init() starts a fresh generation of hooks — which is what makes it safe when a component reconnects — so anything registered before a second call is dropped. Call init() once, then register hooks, then render() or mount().

entries.message: a 'template' or 'element' module (namespaces, elements, slots) was wired after the renderer had already built templates — those never ask it, and keep rendering without it.
entries.fix: Wire it beside the renderer, before the first render.

entries.message: flush() inside a running flush (a hook, a render, or an event one of them fired) does nothing: the DOM updates when this flush ends — nothing failed.
entries.fix: To read the DOM a render made, read it in useLayoutEffect, which runs right after the render.

entries.message: is handed back as it is — it works, but nothing that reads it updates when it changes.
entries.fix: Make it reactive: `import { collections } from '@verajs/store/collections'` and add it to your `wire([…])` call.

entries.message: there is no component being set up. Hooks, `render()` and `mount()` belong to a component's setup, which runs synchronously from `init(this)` and ends at the first `await` — so after an `await` in setup, or later in a handler, there is no component to attach them to.
entries.fix: Setup ends at the first `render()` — to change what is shown later, write to a store, never render() again. Await BEFORE `init(this)`; or create hooks and call `render()` before the first `await` and write what you await into state; or pass the element explicitly: `useEffect(fn, this)`.

entries.message: no renderer is wired, so nothing will appear.
entries.fix: Wire one once, at your app entry: `import { renderer } from '@verajs/renderer'; wire([renderer]);`

entries.message: has re-run for {frames} consecutive frames because it writes state it also reads — this will keep running for as long as the page is open.
entries.fix: Guard the write (`if (next !== state.x) state.x = next`), or move it out of the pass. More than one hook may be involved: a template reading what an effect writes is caught here too. If it is deliberate — an animation driven by one store write per frame — silence it with `allowRenderLoop(this)` from @verajs/core, or drive it with `requestAnimationFrame`.
It receives the flush and decides when to run it — `microtask` (the default) and `frameBudget` are exported for that.

entries.message: registered {hooks} hook(s) but its setup was never committed, so none of them will ever run.
entries.fix: init() opens the setup and one of these closes it: `render(() => html`…`)` for a component with markup, `mount();` for one with none.
To hold one value, use ref(value).

entries.message: this store's source object refused the {operation} — {why}.
entries.fix: A store proxies the object it was given and cannot override what JavaScript declines. Pass a mutable object to createStore, or keep this one outside the store and read it directly.

entries.message: re-entered 50 times and was stopped — it writes state it also reads, and it runs synchronously on every change, so an unguarded write feeds itself.
entries.fix: Guard the write (`if (next !== state.x) state.x = next`), or use `useEffect`, which coalesces.
It runs the function without subscribing — `untrack(() => state.a)`, not `untrack(state.a)`, which reads the property before untrack can do anything about it.

entries.message: renders `{attribute}`, but no directives engine is wired, so that attribute does nothing.
entries.fix: `@verajs/directives` is NOT PUBLISHED YET — `npm i` will 404 — so if this markup came from a demo, remove the attribute or write the behavior yourself for now. When it ships, it is wired once at your app entry: `import { directives } from '@verajs/directives'; wire([renderer, directives]);`

entries.message: declares `static styles`, but nothing is adopting them, so it renders unstyled.
entries.fix: Style adoption lives in `@verajs/styles`. Wire it once at your app entry: `import { styles } from '@verajs/styles'; wire([styles]);`
